records.title: P1 physics: calls to `_emscripten_get_now`
records.text: the trace shows ~3k samples of `_emscripten_get_now` (import `a.b`) on the physics threads and three Box2D pthreads at 100 % inside `wasm-function[102]`. `physicsImportCallsMicrobench.mjs` counts the calls per import in `step_world` with 16.5k circles from the fixture, a single-thread world in Node: **0 calls** to `a.b` per step. The cost comes from the pthread pool (the task system's busy wait), not from the solver. The fix is in the sibling Box2D build repo: it was not touched. **Not-measured** (diagnosis).

records.title: R2 emit type 0
records.text: the plan asked to pick it by hot line. In the after-H9 trace the `emitSpriteQueue` lines are spread out (the hottest is 8 % of self time, `srScaleX[idx]`); there is no line that justifies a hypothesis. **Not-measured.** In the after-campaign trace `emitSpriteQueue` is 26.6 % of pre-render's self time (first on the thread) and it is still spread out: `srScaleX[idx]` 8.1 %, `srAlpha[idx]` 7.7 %, `frameAccum[idx]` 6.5 %, `srAnchorX[idx]` 5.8 %, `srAnchorY[idx]` 4.4 %, `collectorIndex[i]` 4.1 %. Those are the first read of each column per entity, through `collectorIndex` (grid cell order, not index order): the cost is the memory access pattern, not branches by type, so R2 as it stood has nothing to aim at. An idea that does come out of this trace, not measured: emit in entity-index order so those reads are sequential. It changes the queue's row order, so the painter's tie-break would have to be by entity id and not by row, or the checksum will not match.

records.title: X2 pack: a `packInstancedRows` loop specialized by flags
records.text: a loop without the invariant branches (world space, no snap, index list, no type filter, no shadowCast). This is not the H7 hoist. Kernel `gpuQueuePackMicrobench.mjs` (16k rows from the fixture, painter order): sprites **−23.8 %**, casters −46.4 % (fallback path). **Rejected-in-kernel.** **Reversed 2026-10-21 (review E-45):** the loop came back in `4a7fa4c1` with no row. Re-measured on the fixed kernel (one case per `worker_thread`, see X5), with the fast path taken out of the tree against HEAD: without it the pack is **46 % slower** in both queue orders (sprites 3349 → 1808 ops/s cells, casters 2596 → 1399; 0/81 rounds). Predator, 4 ABAB pairs: without it the **renderer is +18.7 % (3.46 → 4.05 ms, 4/4)** and pre-render +3.4 % (3/4). The 09-30 run most likely used the same-process kernel, the one X5 found warming each call kind with the other; that wasn't re-checked. **Kept.**

records.title: R1 stamp: `takeClosest` on (dist, idx) pairs in place
records.text: the same quickselect + quicksort, the same pivots, but swapping dist and idx together instead of sorting a permutation read with `dist[order[i]]`. The same exact result (checksum of kept ids in order). Kernel `shadowStampMicrobench.mjs` with the fixture's casters and lights: `stampLightRange` **−4.1 %**, `takeClosest` **−5.8 %**. Moving two arrays costs more than the indirection. **Rejected-in-kernel.**

records.title: L4 logic: a component cache with one shape per class
records.text: `get` (component getter, 1.7 % of logic) uses one function for every component and class, over `_componentCache` objects whose shape depends on the access order. Variant: the cache starts with every key of the class at `null`, and `neighborCount` reads `Grid._neighborData` without the static getter. Kernel `gameObjectAccessMicrobench.mjs` (real GameObjects, 3 classes) variant **+7.9 %**; gate 4 **+8.5 %**, identical checksum. (A first gate 4 gave +1.8 % but it did not count: the "before" copy was saved in parallel with the edit and already carried half the change. The copies from before each hypothesis are now saved in their own step and checked.) Predator ABAB 8 counterbalanced pairs, owner logic: **4.152 → 4.280 ms (+4.4 %, 6/8 pairs worse)**; the rest does not move. The kernel won and the product loses: with Predator's real classes the pre-populated cache does not pay. **Dropped.** The code went back. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L4/summary.json`.

records.title: X1 pixi: premultiply decal tiles as `Uint32` words
records.text: `copyPremultiplyRgba` was 12 % of Pixi's busy time. Decal tiles are almost all transparent texels with opaque cores: those are copied or zeroed as one word; only a partial alpha does the per-channel math. Little-endian and views aligned to 4 bytes; otherwise the previous path. Kernel `premultiplyMicrobench.mjs` (16 tiles of 128², a decal mix) variant **+44.4 %**, gate 4 **+38.9 %**, identical checksum. Test `premultiplyParity.test.js` (all 65 536 channel × alpha combinations against the per-channel formula, and unaligned views). Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner renderer: 4.146 → 4.260 ms (paired median −0.8 %, 4/8 worse): Predator does not upload tiles every frame. No worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).**

records.title: S3 spatial: inline circle bounds in `rebuildOwnedRows`
records.text: the three spatial workers compute `getColliderBounds` for every entity before seeing whether they touch their rows (13 % of spatial with `rebuildOwnedRows`). For circles the math goes inline with local columns (the same formula as the circle branch of `getColliderBounds`); the other shapes still call the function. This is not the row prefilter (dropped 2026-09-21, +8.7 %): no entity is skipped. Kernel variant **+19.9 %** (on top of S4); gate 4 **+12.9 %**, identical checksum. Test `spatialCircleBounds.test.js` (latched position and extent = `getColliderBounds`, with offsets). Predator ABAB 8 counterbalanced pairs, owner spatial: 5.850 → 5.294 ms (paired median −8.7 %, but only 5/8 pairs better); no worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/S3/summary.json`.

records.title: S4 spatial: a dense candidate count for the stagger skip
records.text: hot line of the trace: `candData[candBaseA] > 0` was 29 % of the self time of `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` (49 % of spatial). Predator uses `maxNeighbors` 1024 and `neighborTickInterval` 15: almost every entity takes the stagger skip and that read lands on the head of a 2 KB row per entity, a cache miss each time. `_candidateCountOf` (one `EntityIdArray` per entity) stores the same count and the skip reads it there. Kernel `spatialWorkerMicrobench.mjs` (3 real `SpatialWorker`s, Predator config, 16.5k entities): variant **+24.0 %**; gate 4 against patched `src/` **+22.6 %** with an identical checksum (neighbor sets + counters). Test `spatialCandidateCount.test.js`. Predator ABAB 8 counterbalanced pairs, owner spatial: **6.119 → 5.133 ms (−13.4 %, 0/8 worse)**; logic +1.2 % (5/8, noise), pre-render −4.7 %, physics −5.2 %. **Kept (product).** A first sitting with a fixed A→B order gave spatial −7.0 % (0/8) but every other worker +2 to +6 % in 5/8 pairs, logic +4.5 % in 6/8: the drift inside the pair always landed on B. That is why the runner now counterbalances (AB, BA, …); that sitting stays in `tests/results/predator-abab/S4-fixed-order/`. In the same kernel, S1 (counters out of the loop) gave +2.6 % and S2 (`Grid` statics to locals) +2.7 %: **rejected-in-kernel** (under 3 %), they did not go in.

records.title: L3 audio: `Atomics.load` before the CAS in `_writeSlot`
records.text: the Predator fixture has all 2048 slots occupied: each `play()` walked all 2048 doing `compareExchange` (it takes the cache line exclusive even when it fails) and dropped. Trace: `_writeSlot` 4.3 % of logic, 92 % on the CAS line. Kernel `audioSlotMicrobench.mjs`: saturated 3 threads **+52.9 %**, saturated 1 thread +43 %, 90 % +6.4 %, 50 % tie, 0 % −19 % (37 → 46 ns per call; at saturation it saves ~7 µs per call). The next-fit variant (`l3`) lost at medium occupancy and was dropped in the kernel. Gate 4 **+51.5 %**. Test `soundSlotClaim.test.js` (4 threads, no slot twice, drops counted). Predator ABAB 8 pairs (baseline with L1), owner logic: **4.015 → 3.778 ms (−6.1 %, 1/8 worse)**; no worker regresses. **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L3/summary.json`.

records.title: L2 contacts: each logic worker validates only its own pairs on the stay
records.text: trace after-campaign (with L1, L3, S4, S3, X1): `_processBox2dCollisionCallbacks` is still 19.1 % of logic's busy time. The 3 logic workers validated **every** pair every frame (two generation `Atomics.load`s + `Transform.active`) but each one fires callbacks only for pairs with `minE % workers === index`: two thirds of the work was so that `isCollidingWith` would answer correctly. Foreign pairs now go to a second table (same columns, a negative value in the `Map`) and are validated when `frameCollisions.has(key)` asks for them, plus a sweep every 30 frames that drops the old ones so the table does not grow. `frameCollisions` becomes a view with `has()` (the only use in the engine and in the demos). Kernel `contactsMicrobench.mjs` (worker 0 of 3, fixture pairs): variant **+80.5 %** in contact and **+72.6 %** dense, with the observable checksum identical (stays fired + how many pairs `has()` answers); the previous checksum used `.size`, which with L2 would count old foreign pairs that had not been swept, and it was changed before measuring. Gate 4 against patched `src/` **+73.3 %** dense, same checksum. Parity `contactPairParity.test.js` passes unchanged: callbacks and `has()` of every pair, every frame, against the Set + two Map reference, with respawns and actives that change, workers 0 and 1 of 3. Predator ABAB 8 counterbalanced pairs (baseline with L1, L3, S4, S3, X1), owner logic: **4.427 → 3.870 ms (−11.7 %, 0/8 pairs worse)**; spatial −1.5 %, physics −6.8 %, renderer −1.7 %, particle −6.8 %, pre-render −2.9 %, none regress. Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.1 %, `GPU_CASTERS` +0.2 %. On pair 1 an audio kernel of ~9 s ran in parallel; logic gave −3.5 % on that pair, inside the range of the rest. **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L2/summary.json`.

records.title: L1 contacts: a dense pair table instead of a `Set` + two `Map`s
records.text: trace after-H9: the contact stay was ~34 % of logic's busy time (`_gensMatch` 29.8 %, hot line = the two `Map.get`s). A `Map` from key to slot and `Uint32Array` columns (min, max, gen of min, gen of max), deleted by swap; the stay walks columns (no `Set` iteration, no unpack, one hash per begin/end, none on the stay except `beginSet`). This is not "Stay without sqrt" (2026-09-21, kernel +553 % / scene +20 %): that kernel measured only the scan; this one runs drain + begin/end + stay on the real `LogicWorker` with Predator's contact pairs. Kernel `contactsMicrobench.mjs`: bench variant **+84 %** (7800 pairs) and **+179 %** (dense); against patched `src/` (gate 4) **+215.9 %** dense. Parity `contactPairParity.test.js` (Set + two Map reference, 120 frames, 2 workers of 3). Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner logic: **6.610 → 4.116 ms (−36.7 %, 0/8 pairs worse)**; spatial −1.1 %, physics −6.4 %, pre-render −5.9 %; renderer +5.8 % and particle +3.6 % with 5/8 pairs worse (noise, they do not block). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.6 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −1.3 %. `contactGensPack.test.js` now pins the two `Uint32Array` columns (still no BigInt and no Float64). **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/L1/summary.json`.

records.title: Bug: contacts with mismatched gens in (max, min) order
records.text: `_applyContactBegin` stored `genA`/`genB` in the order of the Box2D event and the stay compared them against `(minE, maxE)`. If the event arrived (greater, lesser) and the two bodies had different generations (one respawned), the pair was purged while it was still in contact: no `onCollisionStay`, no `onCollisionExit`, `isCollidingWith` false. Fix: they are stored in (min, max) order on begin and compared the same way on end. Test `tests/node/contactGenOrder.test.js`. **Kept (correction).**

records.title: Kernels against a revision: rounds and a verdict by ranges
records.text: at the close of the campaign, `runKernelsVsRev.mjs --vs HEAD --changed` marked `gpuQueuePack` **WORSE (−5.0 %)**, and again **−11.9 %** on a repeat, with the same code on both sides (`gpuQueueLayout.js` unchanged, no imports, identical checksum). Five processes in a row of the same tree gave 1875 to 2128 ops/s: one process per side is not enough for the 3 %. It is now 5 rounds per side with the order alternating, the median, and the verdict also requires that KEEP win (or lose) at least 90 % of the 25 round-against-round comparisons. With that, the same case gives 56 %, a tie. The gate 4s of this campaign were run with a single pass: L1 +215.9 %, L2 +73.3 %, L3 +51.5 %, S4 +22.6 %, S3 +12.9 %, and X1 +38.9 % are above that spread; L4 (+8.5 %) is not, but it was dropped because of Predator.

records.title: Second batch, not measured
records.text: **R3** (emit in entity order) is the same memory-order idea as X5, which did not pay in the browser because of the cross-core effect, and it needs a pre-render kernel with the real worker that does not exist yet. **H11** (repeat under the current protocol) needs that same kernel. **PH1** (`publishPose` without the per-body generation `Atomics.load`): `publishPose` lives in the Emscripten post-js (`weedjsPost.js`) and cannot be imported; it needs a physics-worker harness, and the change touches the generation protocol between logic and physics. **P2** (sway without `Math.sin`): Predator's frequencies are continuous (`1 + rng() * 2` per decoration), so a sine per distinct frequency does not apply; a polynomial sine changes the values in the last digit and is a visual-quality decision, not a measurement. **Not-measured.**

records.title: X6 Pixi: painter radix with one 4-byte histogram and constant passes skipped
records.text: `radixSortIndicesBySortKey` (9 % of Pixi, 98 % from `radixPainterOrder`) did 4 histogram passes and 4 scatter passes, each with indirect key reads. Now: the 4 histograms in one read, and a pass whose byte is the same in every key is skipped (in a stable LSD radix that pass is the identity); sprite keys `round(y) * 128` have a constant low byte. New kernel `painterRadixMicrobench.mjs` (catalog row `painterRadix`; foot-Y keys from the fixture): variant **+75 %** sprites only, **+45 %** with 20 % fractional keys; gate 4 **+48.4 %** (5/5 rounds), identical checksum. Test `radixPainterSort.test.js` against a reference LSD radix (negatives, `-0`, all equal, few values, z bands, subsets, 0–2 slots). Predator ABAB, owner renderer: **4.083 → 3.933 ms (−2.9 %, 2/8 worse)**, just under 3 %; no worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).**

records.title: X5 pack: `packInstancedRows` reading in slot order
records.text: invert the painter list once and walk the queue in order, writing each row at its position. Along the way the kernel `gpuQueuePackMicrobench.mjs` turned out to measure wrong: with the cases in the same process, the shipped function had seen sprites and casters before the clock started and ran almost twice as fast as seeing only one kind of call, which is how the engine uses it (Pixi packs sprites, pre-render packs casters). With each case in its own `worker_thread` (clean JIT), base sprites 1074 ops/s, casters 1315. That reproduced D1 in Node: the function compiled by OSR deopts on `ctx.particleCount = particles` ("Insufficient type feedback for generic named access") until it recompiles. D1a (move that store to a wrapper with no loop) changes nothing: −1.7 % sprites, +5.2 % casters. X5 with the choice at the caller (not a fallback inside the loop: that cost −46 % on casters, the same symptom as X2): kernel **+145 %** sprites; control with the X5 loop in painter order **+50 %** (half the gain is the loop without screen/snap/filter branches, the rest is the order). Gate 4 **+138.1 %**, identical checksum; byte-for-byte parity test on 10 cases. With the queue in cell order (as pre-render builds it) the kernel is still at +73 %. Predator ABAB, owner renderer: **REGRESSION** — renderer +2.5 % (5/8), pre-render **+5.4 % (8/8 worse)**. A trace with X5 shows `packRowsInSlotOrder` at 35.9 % of Pixi, almost what `packInstancedRows` had (38 %): the path runs and it is not faster in the browser. Likely explanation: pre-render writes the queue on another core a moment before, and the cost is bringing those cache lines over, not the read order; in the kernel the data is hot on the same core. **Dropped.** The code went back. The kernel stays with one case per `worker_thread` and `--queue-order cells`.

records.title: S6 spatial: a list of owned entities instead of walking cells
records.text: `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` walked every cell of its rows, read each `gridCounts`, and deduped with `entityProcessedMarker` (14–15 % of the function in the trace). `rebuildOwnedRows` already computes each entity's position: there it builds the dense list of those whose home row is on this worker (row from `Math.fround(posY)`, the same way the search rereads it), and the search walks that list. The per-entity marker and the ownership check are deleted. It also fixes a latent bug: an entity whose home cell was full (`maxEntitiesPerCell`) was never processed and kept stale neighbors. Kernel: variant +4.9 %, gate 4 **tie** (−0.0 %). Test `spatialOwnedList.test.js`: per-frame checksum identical to the cell walk (reconstructed with the inverse diff) over 45 frames with Predator's config, and with a cap of 4 per cell S6 processes all 4000 entities and the old walk does not. Predator ABAB, owner spatial: **4.182 → 3.463 ms (−17.3 %, 0/8 worse)**; renderer +2.8 % (6/8, under 3 %), the rest does not move. The kernel does not see it because it runs the three spatial workers in sequence on one thread; in the scene they run in parallel over the same grid. **Kept (product, and a correction).**

records.title: Q1 logic: `copyTypeActiveListToBuffer` with `TypedArray.set`
records.text: element-by-element copy loop (2.4 % of logic) → `buffer.set(subarray)`, clipped to the space that remains (the old loop silently dropped what did not fit; `set` would throw). Private function of the module: it cannot be injected as a variant, so it was measured directly at gate 4. The kernel `querySystemMicrobench.mjs` used 2048 actives in non-shared lists; it moved to 16384 (Predator) in a `SharedArrayBuffer` and gained a checksum. Gate 4 **+20.9 %** (5/5 rounds), with lists in a SAB **+21.2 %**. New edge test (more matches than space) passes on the old code and the new. Predator ABAB, owner logic, **two sittings: REGRESSION both** — first logic +2.7 % (5/8), spatial +3.8 %, renderer +3.8 %, particle +4.0 % (6/8 each); second logic +3.5 % (6/8), particle +3.2 % (6/8), pre-render +3.6 % (6/8). The A/A control rules out a harness bias. I did not find the mechanism (spatial, renderer, and particle do not run this copy) and the kernel does not reproduce it. **Dropped.** The code went back; the kernel improvements and the test stay.

records.title: G1 logic: neighbors read straight from `Grid._neighborData`
records.text: trace after-L2: `getNeighbor` 8–9 % + `neighborCount` 7 % + `_neighborView` 2 % of logic. `getNeighbor(i)` now reads `Grid._neighborData[offset + 1 + i]` (no per-entity view and no call), and `neighborCount` reads `Grid._neighborData` without the static getter. It was the half of L4 that was never measured alone. Kernel `gameObjectAccessMicrobench.mjs` with a new `neighbors` case (Predator layout: `maxNeighbors` 1024, lists up to 120, a type test per neighbor, like `findACivilianToShoot`): variant **+36.7 %** `tick` and **+31.1 %** `neighbors`; gate 4 **+28.4 %** (5/5 rounds), identical checksum. Test `gameObjectNeighbors.test.js` (against the old view, widths 16 and 32, one id 70000). Contract: `getNeighbor(i)` is valid for `i < neighborCount`; past that it reads the next row. Predator ABAB, owner logic: 8 pairs −5.7 % but only 5/8 better; extended to 16 pairs: **−0.1 % (8/16 worse)**. No worker regresses. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).**

records.title: Predator A/A control
records.text: before continuing after Q1, a sitting of 8 pairs with exactly the same code on both sides. **NEUTRAL**, no bias toward B: logic −6.0 % with 3/8 worse, renderer −3.8 % with 2/8, pre-render −3.0 % with 3/8. With identical code the paired median of logic moves 6 %, and the 6/8 pair rule is what filters it. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/AA-control/summary.json`.

records.title: New method: kernels that do not write `src/`, worktrees, Predator ABAB
records.text: the `*-hyps/` campaigns, the one-sitting A/Bs, and `poolFlowHyps.test.js` were deleted (all of them copied snapshots over `src/`). Kernels call the shipped function or the real worker in Node (`workerHarness.mjs`); variants live in the bench (`methodVariant.mjs` compiles the shipped method with an exact diff). A/B against another revision = a worktree in `../weed-ab/`. Product gate: `runPredatorAbab.mjs`, A B A B, 8 pairs of 10 s/10 s, every worker, a regression only if the paired median is ≥ +3 % **and** ≥ 75 % of the pairs get worse. Full rules in `HOW_WE_MEASURE.md` ("Hypotheses from the trace: the gates"). The new trace (`--trace-cpu`, parser with ms, hot lines, and callers) is in `tests/results/v8-deopt/after-h9/parsed/hot-lines.md`.

records.title: Kernels `--changed` against HEAD
records.text: liquidfun TIE (−1.2 %), liquidfunCouple TIE (+1.9 %), preRenderWorker TIE (−2.3 %). `publishPose` comes out **NEW**: HEAD has no `weedjsBindPoseBench`, so the baseline does not start. The comparison that counts is the gate 4 above, not that row.

records.title: P1 pthread pool 2 against 4
records.text: `wasm-function[102]` is the mailbox wait, so dropping the pool from 4 to 2 (`build_for_weed.bat 2`, LTO full) was the cheap test. Node WASM tests, 51/51. Predator ABAB, A = the saved 4-thread wasm, B = the 2-thread wasm: physics **8.671 → 10.875 ms (+26.2 %, 8/8 worse)**. Renderer −10.4 % and pre-render −9.9 % (0/8 worse): fewer cores burned, but the solver falls behind. **REGRESSION.** The 4-thread wasm went back into `src/box2d/`. The spinner in `solver.c` was not touched: it is not the 61 % of the trace, and removing a thread already showed those pthreads do real work.

records.title: P3 sleeping cells opt-in
records.text: `updateCellSleepingStates` is 12 % of particle, and particle is at ~2 ms. The ceiling is a few tenths of a millisecond, not the bottleneck (pre-render ~8 ms). The overlay and `Grid.isCellSleeping` read it. **The default is not changed.** Not-measured as a speed keep.

records.title: Sway with a grid of 100 frequencies
records.text: the sine that costs is one per blade (`swayBaseAngle * freq + i * 0.1`). The later `Math.cos`/`Math.sin` almost never runs: the grass amplitude is ≤ 0.08. Quantizing the frequency alone is not enough, because the phase `i * 0.1` is still distinct. Kernel in the bench (tolerance 1e-3 against `Math.sin`, checksum of the pass): n=20000, base 1571 ops/s; LUT 1024 +15.6 % (not implemented); 32 frequencies +161.3 %; 100 frequencies +161.1 %. Tie between 32 and 100, 100 stays. `sin(i*0.1)` and `cos(i*0.1)` are built once; per frame there are 100 sines and the loop is a product. Config `particle.swayFrequencyBuckets` default 0: the other scenes stay on `Math.sin`. Predator turns it on and the spawn writes the grid `1 + bucket * (2/99)`. Gate 4 against the previous worker: **1624 → 2194 ops/s (+35.1 %, 100 % of rounds)**, within 1e-3 of the sine. Test `swayBuckets.test.js`. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner particle: **2.027 → 1.813 ms (−10.0 %, 1/8 worse)**. Logic −2.4 %, spatial 0 %, renderer −0.6 %, pre-render −0.1 %. Physics +3.6 % with 5/8 worse (6/8 is required for a regression). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.0 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −0.8 %. **Kept (product).** Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/SWAY/summary.json`.

records.title: P2 sway without `Math.sin`
records.text: Predator spawns 20000 blades of grass with `swayFrequency: 1 + rng() * 2`. A sample of 20000 floats like that has **19979** distinct `float32` values. The sine-of-a-sum identity does not apply. **Not-measured** (not worth it). The sine was not touched.

records.title: E1 4-frame cache in `findACivilianToShoot`
records.text: it is demo, not an engine API. 8 pairs: logic −4.9 % but only 5/8 better. Extended to 16, like G1: **logic −0.1 % (8/16 worse)**. Particle +3.2 % with 10/16 worse, does not block. **NEUTRAL.** The cache changes who the soldier shoots for a few frames and it does not pay. The file went back to git. Not kept.

records.title: PH1 `publishPose` without the generation `Atomics.load` when nothing respawned
records.text: a shared `Int32` (`bodyGenEpoch`) rises in `bumpBodyGeneration`. If it matches the value already seen and the previous frame skipped no body, the publish does not do the per-body load. If it skips (new generation, body not recreated yet), it does not latch the epoch: the next frame stays on the slow path. In-memory kernel +135.9 %. Gate 4 against the `weedjsPost.js` from before the loop: **3234 → 7992 ops/s (+147.1 %, 100 % of rounds)**, identical checksum. Test `publishPoseEpoch.test.js`. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner physics: **8.741 → 8.751 ms (−0.8 %, 4/8 worse, cv 6/13 %)**. Logic −0.6 %, spatial −2.7 %, renderer +0.8 %, particle −4.9 % (2/8, does not block), pre-render −1.5 %. Load: `BODY_COUNT` +0.1 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −0.6 %. **Kept (kernel, product-neutral).** Predator physics does not move: the step is still inside the wasm. The closing trace (`after-t2`) still shows the `Atomics.load` at 41 % of `publishPose`: Predator respawns all the time, the epoch does not stay latched, and the fast path is not the one the scene runs. Numbers in `tests/results/predator-abab/PH1/summary.json`.

records.title: H11 hoist of `ShadowCaster` in `_writeQueueShadow`
records.text: the in-memory variant won +6.9 % (25/25 round pairs) with the same checksum, but gate 4 against the patched `src/` gave **1118 → 1162 ops/s (−0.5 %, 44 % of rounds) TIE**. The gain was recompiling the method, not the hoist. The code went back. **Rejected** at gate 4. There was no Predator. **Re-landed in `4a7fa4c1` and reverted again 2026-10-21 (`bae431b6`, review E-45):** it came back inlined into `emitSpriteQueue` with no row. With the plain `_writeQueueShadow` call restored, against HEAD: emit kernel **+8.6 %** (70/81, checksums equal); Predator, 4 ABAB pairs, owner pre-render **−2.5 %, better in 4/4**. The inline loses.

records.title: R3 emit in entity order
records.text: new kernel `preRenderWorkerMicrobench.mjs` (the real `PreRenderWorker`, collector in cell order, checksum per entity). A variant that sorts the collector by index before the shipped loop: identical checksum, **−68.8 %** ops/s (1153 → 360, 5 rounds). The sort eats the sequential read. **Rejected-in-kernel.** There was no Predator. Same lesson as X5: memory order is not kept from the kernel, and here the kernel did not even win.

records.title: Trace after-keeps and what was measured after
records.text: CPU capture in `tests/results/v8-deopt/after-keeps/` (Predator headed, detailed stats off). The after-l2 was stale: G1, S6, and X6 were already in the tree. The weight order did not change enough to reorder the plan. Logic ~270 ms/s: contacts 15 %, `findACivilianToShoot` 12 %, `get` 8 %, `neighborCount` 8 %, `getNeighbor` 6 %. Spatial ~290 ms/s: `findNeighbors` 41 %, `_publishFilteredNeighbors` 29 %, `rebuildOwnedRows` 20 %. Pre-render ~517 ms/s: `emitSpriteQueue` 23 %, `_displayPose` 11 %, `packInstancedRows` 10 %, `_writeQueueShadow` 3.7 %. Pixi: `packInstancedRows` 39 %, radix 6.6 %. Physics: `wasm-function[102]` 61 % of the pthread threads, `publishPose` 365 ms on the JS thread and 45 % of that function is the generation `Atomics.load`. Deopts: the V8 log had IC lines and **zero** `code-deopt` lines. D1 and D2 still do not reproduce. Map of the shipped binary (no `name` section, LTO) in `tests/results/wasm-map/after-keeps.md`: Chrome's index includes the 18 imports, so `wasm-function[102]` is binaryen's `$84`. The body is the Emscripten mailbox wait (`_emscripten_get_now` + `cmpxchg`), not the spinner in `solver.c`. That spinner is `$74` (chrome 92) and it is not in the top of the trace.

records.title: Max campaign, snapshot
records.text: rev `fc229a21`. Predator A/A 8 pairs, NEUTRAL. Side A median: preRender 7.150 ms, physics 6.836 ms, spatial 6.497 ms, renderer 4.132 ms, logic 3.974 ms, particle 1.665 ms. records.title: Trace wave after the ray keep
records.text:
trace `tests/results/max-campaign/wave5/` against `close/cpu-summary.json`. Spatial is still in `findNeighborsForOwnedEntities` (53.7 %, and the `entityPosData` load is 23 % of that function). Pre-render: `emitSpriteQueue` 21.5 %, `_displayPose` 10.5 %, `collectVisibleEntities` 8.2 %. Pixi: `packInstancedRows` 38.9 %. Physics: `wasm-function[102]` 64.9 % (mailbox, already closed), `wasm-function[285]` 10.5 % (the SAT already lost on Balls). Logic: contacts 14.5 %; `findACivilianToShoot` and `person.js` are demo and do not enter.

Three hypotheses from that trace, Predator headed, stats off:

1. Cache the squared range in the candidate loop when the half-extent repeats. Owner spatial, 4 pairs: **6.077 → 6.760 ms (+9.1 %, 4/4)**. Renderer +9.5 % (3/4), pre-render +3.8 % (3/4). **REGRESSION.** The extra branch on the hot line does not pay: the half-extents change. The file went back to git.
2. With interpolation off, `_displayPose` does not load the previous pose. 4 pairs looked like a keep (−5.4 %, 3/4) but physics and logic, which do not run that function, also fell ~10 %. Extended to 8: pre-render **7.768 → 7.510 ms (−2.0 %, 4/8)**. **NEUTRAL.** The file went back to git.
3. Remove the `|| 0` from `boundsHalfW/H` in `collectVisibleEntities` (17 % of that function in the trace). 4 pairs, owner pre-render: **7.406 → 7.999 ms (+4.8 %, 4/4)**. Renderer +8.0 % (4/4). `GPU_CASTERS` +0.2 %. **REGRESSION.** The file went back to git.

None of them stayed. The wave is not repeated.

records.title: One wait for 3072 `castRayClosest`
records.text: the busy Box2D stress leaves logic at ~50 ms because each ray is its own SAB round trip. Hypothesis: the 3072 rays go into a single `PENDING` and the physics worker calls `castRayClosestBits` in one pass, without waiting between rays. `RayVsBox2dBoxBusyScene` headless, 8 pairs, owner logic: **49.935 → 16.567 ms (−66.8 %, 0/8)**. Physics **6.345 → 4.542 ms (−28.4 %, 0/8)**. `BODY_COUNT` 2800 = 2800. Pre-render +5.2 % is 0.73 ms, under the floor. **Kept (product).** `Box2d.castRayClosestBatch`. `tests/results/predator-abab/ray-batch/summary.json`.

records.title: QueryAABB wake on the LiquidFun query
records.text: the same stress, headless, 4 pairs. A without `pumpQueryWake`, B with the wake always armed. Physics **11.405 → 11.746 ms (+4.0 %, 3/4)**, logic **+15.1 % (4/4)**, `BODY_COUNT` 4 = 4. The wake is what makes it more expensive. The fix (arm `waitAsync` only after serving a QueryAABB, so that stress does not go back to 16 ms) against the always-armed wake: physics **12.929 → 12.438 ms (−2.9 %, 2/4)**, logic −1.7 % (2/4). It does not reach 3 %. Particle +8.2 % is 0.045 ms, under the 3 ms floor, and does not count. **Dropped.** Both files went back to git. `tests/results/predator-abab/lf-query-wake/` and `lf-query-lazy/`.

records.title: Polygon SAT, cut the second axis
records.text: `wasm-function[285]` is `b2CollideTask` (task table, no symbol; the body carries `B2_CONTACT_RECYCLE_COS_ANGLE` 0.98 and `1.5 * B2_LINEAR_SLOP`). Hypothesis: in `b2CollidePolygons` the second `b2FindMaxSeparation` is unnecessary if axis A already cleared the speculative band. Rebuild LTO full, 4 threads, Node WASM tests 71/71. Balls headed ABAB 8 pairs, owner physics: **8.212 → 8.443 ms (+4.6 %, 6/8 worse)**, `BODY_COUNT` 9004 = 9004. **Dropped.** The wasm went back to git and so did the C in the sibling repo. Predator was not run: this wave's rule already requires a revert when either scene rises 3 %. `tests/results/predator-abab/sat-early-balls/summary.json`.

records.title: Interleaved record, write and read on Predator
records.text: `emitSpriteQueue` writes x, y, scale, rotation, alpha, and texture into an 8-float block of the SAB, and `packInstancedRows` reads it. The read-only microbench (+25.5 %) does not count. Primary `max(preRender, renderer)`. Eight pairs: the paired primary −5.9 % but only 5/8 better, so it was extended to 16. On 16 pairs the primary is **7.604 → 7.688 ms, paired −3.8 %, 6/16 worse** (it does not reach 12/16). Renderer **+8.1 % (12/16 worse, cv 11 %)**. `BODY_COUNT` −0.0 %, `GPU_CASTERS` +0.5 %. **Dropped.** The extra write eats the read, and Pixi comes out more expensive. The WASM pack was not compiled: the record did not stay in the tree. The four files went back to git. `tests/results/predator-abab/hot-record/summary.json`.

records.title: Neighbor publish in shared memory
records.text: the kernel with a copy and a fixed 256 MB had lost on Predator. This form does not copy the row: poses, candidates, and `neighborData` live in a `WebAssembly.Memory` the size of the scene (128 KB header, `uint16` ids). Kernel +118 % ops/s, same checksum (`spatialPublishWasmMicrobench.mjs`, 386 pages). Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner spatial: **7.936 → 6.637 ms (−14.6 %, 0/8 worse)**. Logic +1.5 % (4/8), pre-render +1.1 % (6/8, under 3 %), physics −0.7 % (cv 19 %). Load: `BODY_COUNT` −0.0 %, `GPU_CASTERS` +0.7 %. **Kept (product).** `src/util/spatialPublishMemory.js`, `src/workers/spatialPublishClient.js`.

records.title: renderOnly particles
records.text: `ParticleEmitter` accepts `renderOnly: true` (default off). A shared `Int32` counts how many there are. If it is 0, integrate and emit do not read the column. If it is > 0, those particles age on the CPU and do not integrate motion or enter the sprite emit; the look stays on the compute layer that already packs them. Test `particleFlatGravity.test.js`. Integrate stress, one run, default: particle 2.460 → 2.276 ms, preRender 4.021 → 4.135 ms (+2.8 %, under 3 %). This is not a new GPU integrator: if the shader does not move the pose, the sprite is not drawn.

records.title: QueryAABB across frames
records.text: a synchronous `queryAABB` from logic waited for the physics worker's next `requestAnimationFrame`. Snapshot: logic 16.597 ms, BODY_COUNT 201. With `Atomics.waitAsync` the logic step falls to 0.150 ms (it ate the 3 ms floor; the baseline was above it). Physics 0.149 → 0.109 ms. Predator ABAB 8 pairs, owner logic: **NEUTRAL** (logic +0.7 %, 4/8). Nothing regresses. **Kept** on the query stress, Predator product neutral. Files: `box2dQueryAabbImpl.js`, `physicsHostImpl.js`, `weedjsPost.js`.

records.title: Neighbor row
records.text: Predator `maxNeighbors` 1024. Readers walk `neighborCount`. `visualRange` reaches 400 with 32 entities per cell, so the list can pass 64. **The cap is not lowered.**

records.title: Interleaved pack record
records.text: microbench of 8 fields × 16384 rows, the read only, columns against one block. **+25.5 %** ops/s. It does not include the extra write on emit. Without that write measured on Predator there is no second layout. **Not-measured** as a scene keep. `tests/bench/hotRecordMicrobench.mjs`.

records.text: uint16 kernel, stride 1025, 48 candidates, same SAB: **+126.1 %** ops/s, identical checksum (`tests/bench/spatialPublishWasmMicrobench.mjs`). Wired into `SpatialWorker` (256 MB memory, candidates inside, pose copy, write back to `Grid.neighborData`). Predator 8 pairs, owner spatial: **REGRESSION** — logic +9.3 % (6/8), preRender +3.6 % (6/8). The worker went back to git. The kernel stays in the bench. The pack was not compiled: the interleaved record is not shipped.

records.title: Worker count
records.text: Predator headed, stats off. Spatial 2 against 1, 8 pairs: spatial 6.444 → 4.142 ms (−35.5 %, 0/8) but renderer +8.1 % (7/8). **REGRESSION.** Spatial 3 against 1, 4 pairs: spatial −52.2 % and particle +6.2 % (3/4). **REGRESSION.** Logic 3 against 2, 4 pairs: logic −15.8 % and particle +7.1 % (3/4). **REGRESSION.** Logic 1 against 2, 4 pairs: logic +80.8 % (4/4), spatial +7.5 %, preRender +4.8 %. **REGRESSION.** The default stays at 1 spatial and 2 logic.

records.title: LiquidFun contact alias filter
records.text: `FindParticleContacts` walks the 9 neighboring cells without looking at the particle's real cell. Two diagonal cells can land in the same bucket and the pair is pushed twice. The fix marks only those aliases and filters the cell there. Pthread pool pinned at 4 (`-DBOX2D_PTHREAD_POOL_SIZE=4`, LTO full). The previous sitting does not count: the machine was busy (Balls reached 35 ms). This sitting, the same build with and without the filter, detailed stats off. Microbench (warmup discarded): 1 worker 2.796 → 3.252 ms (+16.3 %); 4 workers 2.718 → 2.815 ms (+3.6 %); contacts 25328 = 25328. Balls headed 2×10 s/10 s, physics primary: 7.026 → 7.092 ms (+0.9 %), `BODY_COUNT` 9004, `AWAKE_COUNT` 9000. LiquidFun stress headless 2×8 s/10 s, physics primary: 4.610 → 4.681 ms (+1.5 %), `BODY_COUNT` 3, both sides above the 3 ms floor. **Kept (hygiene).** It is not a speed keep: the 1-worker path comes out more expensive and the 4-worker path barely clears 3 %. Both scenes tie. Numbers: `tests/results/lf-contact-dedup/quiet-*.json`.

records.title: Math-allocation audit, scoreboard vs `5ef9775e`
records.text:
`pnpm bench:scoreboard --vs 5ef9775e` aborts in lockstep. Balls never reaches 9004 active transforms inside 120 s: this tree stopped at 3004 and then 2404, and the pre-audit `src/` in the worktree stopped at 2104. Same harness, same `setTimeout` spawn. Lockstep was skipped and the 38 catalog rows were run (`--skip-lockstep`, detailed stats off). That sitting’s product line said nine rows were FAIL or WORSE. Three of those are under the 3 ms floor (spatial, queryAabb, meshFillMoving), which is not a regression. The six WORSE rows were re-run the same day, same anchor, same flags, `--only ray,rayVsBox2d,liquidfunQuery,tilemap,decalPremultiply,painterRadix`. `ray.js`, `tileMap.js`, `pinGpuTexture.js`, and `sortIndexByKey.js` are unchanged since `5ef9775e`.

The rerun: ray kernel 1,511,214 → 1,517,427 ops/s (+0.4 %). ray scene logic0 was 4.405 → 4.652 ms (+5.6 %) on that pair, then a scene-only pair was 4.658 → 4.561 ms (−2.1 %), **TIE**. `RAYCAST_COUNT` was 3072 on both trees and `RAYCAST_MS` was 4.090 → 4.036 ms. rayVsBox2d **TIE** (kernel +1.5 %, logic0 −0.8 %). liquidfunQuery physics 12.576/13.252 → 12.281/11.245 ms (−8.9 %), the opposite sign of the first sitting’s +6.3 % on overlapping samples. tilemap **TIE** (kernel +2.9 %, logic0 −1.5 %; the −37.2 % did not reproduce). decalPremultiply kernel +6.3 % and painterRadix kernel −2.7 %, both the other side of a 4 % first-sitting swing, source unchanged. **No code change.** None of the six is a stable regression. The first board’s Balls physics tie (8.209 → 8.127 ms) and visPoly keep (9.035 → 7.396 ms) stand. `productVerdict` no longer counts a step-floor FAIL as “do not claim a better WeedJS”. The row itself stays FAIL, as the protocol requires.

records.title: Balls spawn all at once, scoreboard vs `5ef9775e`
records.text: `spawnBalls` no longer schedules 9000 `setTimeout`s. The 9000 balls are created in `createNewGame` before the flush, so both sides of the board see the same init. Lockstep balls/liquidfun/lfstress/particles **PASS**. Full catalog, detailed stats off, gameplay headed 5×10 s/10 s. Balls physics **8.013 → 7.997 ms (−0.2 %)**, `BODY_COUNT` 9004/9004, `AWAKE_COUNT` 9000/9000. **TIE.** Product line: six rows FAIL/WORSE, do not claim a better engine. The scene primaries that are worse: liquidfun physics +3.3 %, liquidfunCouple physics +4.5 % (kernel −8.3 %), decalBlit pixi +4.5 %. Kernel-only WORSE: decalPremultiply −4.7 %, publishPose −9.3 %. visPoly preRender −16.5 % and swayBuckets kernel +14.7 % are keeps. This commit is not faster than `5ef9775e`.

records.title: Mesh API trace
records.text: headed `meshApiStressScene`, `--src`, detailed stats off, 10 s / 10 s. Cohorts: 600 rigid fans, 120 deform grids (24×16), 400 ropes, 400 UV quads, 8 planes, 8 stars, 200 outset boxes. `BODY_COUNT` 200 (fill only). Trace (`--trace-cpu`, summary from 10 s for 10 s): pixi busy time is `updateBuffer` 50.3%, `writeExplicitTriCorners` 25.3%, `rewriteExplicitMeshCorners` 4.5%, `uploadPoseTable` 4.1%. Logic busy time is the scene `_wave` 59.3%, then `_copyVerts` 9.5%. Three Box2D threads sit in `wasm-function[102]` while physics `STEP_MS` is 0.16 ms. They were left alone. Kernel, same sitting, checksum first: pose-table run walk 2.91 k → 11.1 k ops/s (**+282%**) on 122880 instances; hoisted corner rewrite 2.16 k → 2.78 k ops/s (**+28.5%**) on 30720 UV triangles, every float matched; `writeVertices` without unary plus **−8.1%**, not shipped. Headed renderer **3.779 → 3.029 / 2.762 ms** (median of the two changed windows 2.896 ms, **−23.4%**). Baseline above 3 ms. Second changed window under 3 ms, allowed because it is cheaper. Logic under 3 ms every window, no verdict. One baseline window, not counterbalanced. **Kept.** The scene number is both edits. `meshFillMoving` after the edits is renderer 0.893 ms, `BODY_COUNT` 6500, under the floor, not a pair. Report: `[MESH_API_TRACE_REPORT.md](./reports/MESH_API_TRACE_REPORT.md)`.

records.title: Math-allocation audit, visibility hygiene
records.text: H-04 hoists the constant end direction in `angularSweep.js`. H-06 uses the first-order ε expansion for the pre/post samples. H-05 uses angle addition in `emitArcVertices` (at most 4 steps). The polygon gate, stated before the edit, is 1e-4 world units against a fixture snapped from the old sweep; the test passes. H-08 drops `%` from `normalizeAngleSigned`: bit-identical on `(−π, π)`, at most 1 ulp on `[−3π, 3π]`. No scene. The Predator trace names none of these functions. **Kept (hygiene).** H-09 (squared distance before the occluder cull) was **not shipped**: it is the same extra branch that lost 4/4 on 2026-10-06, and there is no vehicle.

records.title: Math-allocation audit, H-15 castAll sort
records.text: one headless baseline each, `--src`, detailed stats off, warmup 10 s, measure 10 s. `RayStressScene`: logic0 **4.906 ms**, `BODY_COUNT` 2000, and the scene calls `Ray.castAll` with `maxHits` 4 among line-of-sight, linecast, and `cast`. records.title: Audio slot scan, per-bus list and quietest cache
records.text:
a full bus was walking every slot up to the high-water mark, including other buses. Each bus now keeps the slots it holds, plus the quietest voice and the second quietest, in a tail of the channel SAB. A shot that is not louder than the cached minimum drops after one read. A louder shot claims that slot and promotes the second. A miss walks that bus's list only. The worklet's free sites update the list. `PLAYS_PER_TICK` was raised from 800 to **1200** and frozen. Headed, `--src`, detailed stats off, one window each side, warmup 10 s, measure 10 s: logic0 **8.806 → 0.278 ms (−96.8 %)**. Baseline is above 8 ms. The fast side is under 8 ms, which the campaign rule allows when the baseline cleared it and the step got cheaper. `BODY_COUNT` 0 / 0. Kernel `audioSlotMicrobench.mjs` storm case, 5 alternating rounds, checksum matched (drop count and the voices left on each bus): **20,916 → 261,576 ops/s (+1150 %)**, 5/5. The no-channel occupancy cases in that same run went through a bench wrapper and are not the shipped path (occ50 −10 %, occ90 −8 % there). `soundManager.test.js`, the mixer tests, and `soundSlotClaim.test.js` pass. **Kept.** Predator was not the pair: this function was 4.3 % of logic there.

Main thread busy is 19 ms/s. `getActiveSlotCount` is the top function, **20.1 ms in the 10 s window** (10.6 % of that light thread, 97 % of it the `for` over `maxSlots`). Kernel `audioMetricsMicrobench.mjs`, 2048 slots / 128 playing, checksum 128: **42,732 ops/s** (23 µs/call) and `readPlayingVoices` **49,921 ops/s**. At 60 Hz the scan is about 1.4 ms of main per second. There is no worker `STEP_MS` for that call. **Screened.** No counter was added.

The audio worklet does not appear in the trace (no `process`, `mixVoice`, or `audioMixerProcessor` samples). Kernel `audioMixerMicrobench.mjs`, checksum of one quantum: 32 voices 37,289 ops/s, 128 voices **9,527 ops/s**, 512 voices 2,322 ops/s, 128 voices inside a 2048-slot table **9,271 ops/s** (−2.7 % vs the 128-slot mix, under 3 %). The empty-slot walk is not the mix. **Dropped.** The panel stayed closed during the trace. `audioPanelMicrobench.mjs`, checksum 200 rows: update at 0 voices 5,380 ops/s, at 200 voices 5,887 ops/s. Not a worker step. Three Box2D threads sit in `wasm-function[102]` at 1000 ms/s while physics `STEP_MS` is 0.076 ms. They were left alone.

records.title: Ease dispatch, switch vs else-if vs object
records.text: `applyParticleEase` stays a switch. The kernel `tests/bench/easeDispatchMicrobench.mjs` times that shipped function against the same curve bodies written as an else-if chain and as a plain object of functions keyed by the numeric ease id. A direct call to the one curve, with no id test, is the ceiling on the single-ease rows. `src/` was not edited. Seed `0xe35e0001`, 4096 inputs, three fresh isolates per cell, `timeIt` held the 3 ms sample floor. Checksums match the shipped function on every cell (lerp `1543583917`, quad-in `1054200789`, bounce `1369305495`, mixed `69436109`). Median ops/s: lerp switch 107.5 M (9.3 ns), else-if 101.9 M (−5.2%), object 307.7 M, direct 1004 M. Quad-in switch 113.3 M (8.8 ns), else-if 108.0 M (−4.8%), object 314.7 M, direct 944 M. Bounce switch 56.5 M (17.7 ns), else-if 54.8 M (−3.1%), object 147.4 M, direct 279 M. Mixed ids, uniform over 0..13: switch 57.2 M (17.5 ns), else-if 53.8 M (−6.0%), object 53.2 M (−7.0%). The else-if chain is about 1 ns slower. The object is about 3× the switch when the id does not change, and the direct call is about 3× the object again, so the lookup is not free. When the id changes every call the object loses the three rounds by about 1 ns. This loop is tiny, so a small function can inline here; `Tween.tick` and particle integrate are large and were not re-timed. **Screened.** No scene. Report: `tests/results/ease-dispatch/kernel.json`.

records.title: Audit hygiene, kernel vs `5c986922`
records.text: the audio-thread lock, chain scratch capacity, mesh free-span rescan, texture sequence lock, chain ray local space, `setPlane` counts, `getMetrics(out)`, camera `setAngle`, channel lookup, and chain mass. No scene. Kernel `tests/bench/auditFixMicrobench.mjs`, five alternating processes, `timeIt` samples above 3 ms, same iteration count both sides. Working tree versus HEAD `src/` in `../weed-ab/HEAD-5c986922`. Checksums match except free-span (the new merge joins the neighbor the old scan left behind) and chain mass (disk mass versus 0). Medians: one-shot audio quantum 162,214 → 203,438 ops/s (+25.4%, 25/25); play on a live bus 3,641,064 → 2,232,915 (−38.7%, 0/25); sized chain scratch check 346,340,337 → 259,542,513 (−25.1%, 0/25); free span 160,294,943 → 126,540,232 (−21.1%, 0/25, different checksum); texture word union 3,458,173 → 3,034,855 (−12.2%, 0/25); `locateView` 16,150,132 → 37,513,599 (+132%, 25/25); chain ray plus pick 34,583 → 38,675 (+11.8%, 25/25); `setPlane` 557,507 → 601,549 (+7.9%, 22/25); `getMetrics` 51,152 → 51,387 (+0.5%, 16/25); `setAngle` 184,479,154 → 188,361,755 (+2.1%, 18/25); channel handle 69,299,749 → 69,949,962 (+0.9%, 14/25); chain `syncMass` 43,501,903 → 66,232,842 (+52%, 25/25, different checksum); `updateTexture` union 1,798,103 → 2,229,406 (+24%, 21/25). Kernel keeps are the one-shot quantum, `locateView`, and the chain query. The play path, the scratch check, the free, and the texture word union are kernel losses. `setPlane` and the picture upload are above 3% on the median and short of 23 of 25 rounds. No worker `STEP_MS`. Not an engine-wide speed claim. Report: `tests/results/audit-fixes/compare.json`.

records.title: Frame phase, E-24
records.text: Predator headed, `--src`, detailed stats off, warmup 10 s, then 5 s / 302 frames. Not a speed pair. Step durations from the same stamps: physics 7.77 ms, pre-render 7.81 ms, spatial 6.45 ms, logic0 4.85 ms, logic1 4.56 ms, renderer 4.72 ms, particle 1.33 ms. The two longest overlapped on every frame. Particle finishes in 1.33 ms and does not start another frame; the rest of the 16.7 ms is the vsync. **Answered.** The idle E-01 measured is the display period, and the workers are not taking turns inside it. A capture that sampled after the publish is discarded: it printed a −16.8 ms lead because main's `requestAnimationFrame` is registered first. records.title: Sprite label strings, E-07 and `_sortPrefix` realloc, E-08
records.text: both kept as hygiene. **E-07:** four unconditional per-row template-literal strings in `emitSpriteQueue` (read only in two warning branches) became a frozen numeric tag table and `formatAnimLabel`, called only on the warn path. Predator ABAB, 4 counterbalanced pairs, 10 s / 10 s, stats off, `--owner preRender`: preRender **6.855 → 6.797 ms, +1.3 %, 2/4 worse, NEUTRAL**; load closed (`BODY_COUNT` +0.1 %, `GPU_CASTERS` −0.8 %); physics +3.7 % reported, not blocking. `animLabelNoPerRowString.test.js` 9/9 (checksum is the warning text); suite 1084/1084. **E-08:** `tmp.length = n` on a plain Array reallocates the backing store; the scratch is now sized once with geometric headroom (`sortPrefixNoRealloc.test.js` 9/9, which caught a first fix, `new Array(Math.max(n, 16))`, that still reallocated). No sitting: hygiene by construction and the function had no timer until E-29. Reopened 2026-10-21 (see the E-08 row above). Reports: `[reports/E-07-anim-label-strings.md](./reports/E-07-anim-label-strings.md)`, `[reports/E-08-sort-prefix-realloc.md](./reports/E-08-sort-prefix-realloc.md)`.

records.title: Neighbor cell lookup, E-13
records.text: rejected by premise inspection, no scene. The function is reached only in the `else` of `skinCanReuse` and after the neighbour stagger `continue`; Predator runs `neighborTickInterval: 15`, so 14 of every 15 entities exit before the cell walk and the Verlet skin captures most of the rest. The assumed ~16.5 k `Map.get` per frame does not happen. A `spatialCellRebuildMicrobench.mjs` driving the real worker was written and deleted, because `setActiveList` did not reach the worker's view and every counter read zero. Report: `[reports/E-13-neighbor-cells-rejected.md](./reports/E-13-neighbor-cells-rejected.md)`.

records.title: `box2dWorkerCount` sweep, E-04b
records.text: `4` confirmed, the 2026-10-01 confound resolved. Balls (9004 bodies / 9000 awake), three independent sweeps, primary `physics_STEP_MS`, load `BODY_COUNT` and `AWAKE_COUNT` (closed at 0.0 % spread). 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 workers: run A 10.723 / 7.541 / 6.411 / **5.763**, run B 10.792 / 7.945 / 6.521 / **5.795**, run C 10.610 / 7.350 / 6.315 / **5.550** ms. 1 → 4 workers is a 1.86× speedup; physics pays 5.0 ms to save workers and the largest offsetting saving in any other worker is 0.12 ms, so no trade exists. Sleeping-heavy scene (9000 bodies, 0 awake): 0.706 / 0.683 / 0.682 / 0.661 ms, a 6.7 % spread, all under the 3 ms floor (reported, not judged). `STEP_MS` was charging the old pool experiment for lost parallelism, not for removed spin. Report: `[reports/E-04b-box2d-worker-count.md](./reports/E-04b-box2d-worker-count.md)`.

records.title: Pack and sort in pre-render on Predator, E-05
records.text: dropped, Predator's `'pixi'` override stays. Predator ABAB, 4 counterbalanced pairs, 10 s / 10 s, stats off; A = `preRender`/`preRender`, B = shipped `pixi`/`pixi`; primary `max(preRender, pixi)` named before the run. Renderer **2.245 ms (A) against 3.542 ms (B)**, preRender 7.412 against 6.475 ms, max **7.412 (A) against 6.475 ms (B)**. The mechanism worked (renderer −1.30 ms, −36.6 %, 4/4) and the bottleneck moved the wrong way (max 12.6 % worse, 0/4). The runner said `FAIL (load)` on `DECAL_TILES_DIRTY` 0.8 → 1.0 (E-32; now `NEUTRAL (below floor)`). It reconciles the 2026-09-27 shared-pack tie, when pre-render was larger (11.8 ms). No `src/` or scene change. Report: `[reports/E-05-pack-in-prerender.md](./reports/E-05-pack-in-prerender.md)`.

records.title: Load gate floor, E-32
records.text: harness fix, kept. `DECAL_TILES_DIRTY` read 0.8 → 1.0 tiles per frame in E-05 and 1.1 → 0.8 in E-17, failing both pairs on about 25 % deltas of a mean below one tile. `LOAD_GATE_MIN = { ACTIVE_PARTICLES: 1000, DECAL_TILES_DIRTY: 8 }` mutes a key only when both medians are under the floor; the 5 % band does not widen (a draft that widened it to the key's own noise was rejected). `tests/bench/readjudicateAbab.mjs` recomputed all 9 recorded Predator sittings from `summary.json`: only E-17 (now `REGRESSION`, owner preRender +3.1 %, 3/4, cv 7 %) and E-05 (now `NEUTRAL (below floor)`) changed, and every earlier verdict (E-07, H-02 ×2, H-10, H-14, H-19) is unchanged. `decideAbabLoadGate.test.js` pins the floor, the band, the 50 % cv fail, and that a real consistent shift still fails.

records.title: Shadow stamp: E-29 timers, E-16 and E-17
records.text: **E-29 kept (instrumentation):** `VISIBLE_LIGHTS_MS` and `STAMP_LIGHTS_MS` (slots 19 and 20, stride 19 → 21) were added; `STAMP_LIGHTS_MS` is a sub-timer of `SHADOW_Q_MS` and the two must not be added. `--no-collect-detailed-stats` reads exactly 0.000. Predator headed, stats on, two runs: `VISIBLE_LIGHTS_MS` 0.055 / 0.041 ms, `STAMP_LIGHTS_MS` 0.052 / 0.048 ms, about 0.095 ms total (about 1.3 % of the pre-render step); `STAMP_LIGHTS_MS` is about 2 % of `SHADOW_Q_MS` (0.048 / 2.059). The first run's `STEP_MS` 12.160 is a warm-up outlier. **E-16 (incremental or sharded stamp) rejected on premise** by that reading: the only part a shard could attack is about 0.05 ms, about 0.7 % of pre-render, a quarter of the 3 % bar; no scene. It also bounds E-08's `_sortPrefix` at about 0.7 %. **E-17 (cache the stamp cell index) FAIL (load), reverted:** kernel 0.263 → 0.147 ms (+79.2 %), which is 1.79 % of the pre-render step; Predator, 4 ABAB pairs, stats off, `--owner preRender`: **preRender 7.472 → 7.794 ms, +3.1 %, 3/4 worse**, the opposite sign, with the runner verdict `FAIL (load)` on `DECAL_TILES_DIRTY` 1.1 → 0.8 (E-32). The 52.3 KB `Int32Array` traded ALU work for memory-bound work. After E-32 the sitting reads `REGRESSION`. Reports: `[reports/E-29-pre-render-light-timers.md](./reports/E-29-pre-render-light-timers.md)`, `[reports/E-17-stamp-grid-cell-cache.md](./reports/E-17-stamp-grid-cell-cache.md)`.

records.title: Pair-key comment, E-26
records.text: hygiene, kept, no measurement. The comment claiming a `Float64Array` key was attached to nothing (`Float64Array` has one hit in `logicWorker.js`, the comment itself; the key lives in a `Map`), and it manufactured the E-10 hypothesis. The note moved to `entityIdWidth.js` on `packPair`, states the signedness fact, cites E-10's number, and forwards to E-27. Suite 1125 → 1131. Report: `[reports/E-26-pair-key-comment.md](./reports/E-26-pair-key-comment.md)`.

records.title: Contact pair key, E-10 and E-27
records.text: E-10 rejected in kernel, no `src/` change. The kernel's own premise probe swept all **715,838,805** `pack16` keys and found **0 boxed**, range `[-2,147,450,879, 2,147,483,646]`, 25 % negative, because JS `<<` is 32-bit signed. Timing 42.15 M against 42.05 M ops/s (−0.23 %), checksums equal. A 2026-10-20 review note (M10) says the V8 premise was backwards: pointer compression makes Smis 31-bit, the sweep ran in Node (no compression), and in Chrome every key with minE at or above 16384 is a HeapNumber once it enters `_pairSlot` or `frameCollisions`. The Node result stands for Node; the Chrome cost is E-54. E-27 asked whether `entityIdWidth: 32` costs anything (falsifier: within 3 % of the 16-bit path), using the same kernel unmodified, 64 k entities: `PAIR0` pack16 plus `Set` 7,007,659 ops/s, `PAIR1` float-multiply plus `Set` 3,422,003 (0.49×), `PAIR3` packCantor plus `Set` (ships at 32-bit) 4,061,285 (0.58×). **The falsifier fails:** the 32-bit option is about 1.73× slower on pack-then-`Set.has` and 2.40× on packing alone. Cantor against the other 32-bit encoding is −1.8 %, so the entire gap is the key becoming a double. `PAIR_COUNT` (logic stats slot 16, stride 16 → 17) was added as the missing denominator; no scene. Reports: `[reports/E-10-pair-key-smi.md](./reports/E-10-pair-key-smi.md)`, `[reports/E-27-entity-id-width-32.md](./reports/E-27-entity-id-width-32.md)`.

records.title: Browser-tree CPU, E-34
records.text: the process-wide Chrome sum is discarded. This samples the benchmark process and its children. Balls headless, `--src`, 8 s/8 s, one window, load 9004/9000. Physics **6.37 ms / 2.02 cores at 4 workers**, **16.33 ms / 1.40 cores at 1**. The step check passes. The whole tree at 4 workers is 2.02 cores. No Emscripten change. Report: `[reports/E-34-browser-tree-cpu.md](./reports/E-34-browser-tree-cpu.md)`.

records.title: Neighbor read shape, E-15 sitting 2
records.text: closed, no scene, no wasm edit. Kernel `e40NeighborReadShape.mjs`, 17 556 entities, stride 1025, 32 ids, each shape its own thread, `timeIt` floor held. Dense control strided **1.472 ms** / packed **0.499 ms** (delta 0.973). One logic worker, 2 195 ids: id-order **+0.015 ms**, shuffled **−0.012 ms**, id-order plus two position loads **−0.003 ms**, shuffled plus those loads **−0.026 ms**, 64 lights **−0.0003 ms**. Bar was 0.15 ms on the position-load shape (3 % of logic0 at 4.85 ms). A prior pass of that shape printed +0.148 ms and did not repeat.
